blocks.content: **Methodology**: This document was produced by manually examining all 845 commits in chronological order using `git log --oneline --reverse`, then reading the actual source file changes and the current source tree of each significant commit. Feature families are grouped by domain. Every entry includes a description, the commit(s) where it was introduced, the current API surface, use-case context, and usage examples drawn directly from the source code.

blocks.text: **Introduced:** `eabf2b48` (Version 1 — quadratic bezier with WebGPU) **Matured:** `97ca0a33` (Redefined Structure), `652084c6` (Component redesign), `d82d1f59` (New SceneComposer)

**Description:** Retiam is built on a WebGPU rendering backend accessed via the browser's `navigator.gpu` API. The initial commit bootstrapped a stateless rendering context capable of drawing a quadratic Bézier curve entirely on the GPU. Over subsequent commits, this evolved into a full ECS (Entity-Component-System) architecture with a frame graph, PPLL order-independent transparency, shadow passes, and a deferred compositing pipeline.

**Description:** `SceneComposer` is the top-level GPU orchestrator. It owns and manages the WebGPU `GPUDevice`, the `GPUCanvasContext`, and the render loop. Multiple lightweight `Scene` instances can be stacked inside a single `SceneComposer`, each rendered and composited in z-index order — similar to how Adobe After Effects handles compositions.

blocks.text: **Introduced:** `41ef7f92` (frame graph skeleton), `af63dfab` (frame graph integrated) **Expanded:** `8b3c10ac` (PPLL), `a38152d8` (custom pass and post-process), `464b3341` (RenderTarget)

**Description:** The renderer uses a directed acyclic frame graph where each node is a `Pass`. Passes declare texture dependencies (read/write), and the graph resolves execution order automatically with topological sorting and pass culling. This allows advanced techniques like order-independent transparency, shadow maps, feedback textures, and custom post-process effects to compose cleanly without manual ordering.
**Introduced:** `4f9c4263` (offline renderer, simplified config API) **Updated:** `5829c285` (made instance-specific), `809d6034` (static config removed)
**Description:** `RenderConfig` is a per-`SceneComposer` data class controlling global rendering quality parameters.

cells.text: Max PPLL transparent layers per pixel

blocks.text: 1.6 PPLL — Per-Pixel Linked List Order-Independent Transparency

**Description:** Standard alpha blending requires back-to-front draw order. Retiam implements GPU-based Per-Pixel Linked Lists (PPLL) using WebGPU compute shaders and atomic storage buffers. Each fragment writes itself into a linked list at its screen pixel. A composite pass then sorts and blends all layers per-pixel, producing correct order-independent transparency.

**Description:** A GPU-accelerated SVG path renderer — the most powerful 2D primitive in Retiam. **Description:** Retiam Studio is a browser-based live coding IDE. Provides a real-time development environment with Monaco Editor, TypeScript IntelliSense, and multiple interactive widgets.
TypeScript language server with auto-complete, hover docs, and type checking. Retiam type definitions are dynamically injected into the Monaco environment.
Code changes auto-run without page reload. The scene resets, camera and pointer state are preserved, and animations fast-forward to the previous timeline position.
When live-updating code, the editor captures the current camera pose and restores it after the scene resets, preventing disorienting camera jumps.
Inline color swatches appear next to `Color` values in the editor. Clicking opens an interactive color picker that updates the code and live-previews changes.
Hovering over a number literal shows a floating scrub slider widget. Dragging updates the value in real-time without typing.
A 2D joystick widget appears when editing `Vec2`/spatial parameters, allowing interactive spatial tuning with direct scene feedback.
A visual curve browser for `Rate.*` functions. Hover over a `rate_func` argument to see a preview of the easing curve and select from all presets.
Tracks a history of parameter edits made via interactive widgets. Provides a "pre-tune reset" checkpoint to revert to the state before tuning began.
A code-aware property inspector that shows all scene entity properties, identified by parsing the TypeScript AST, and allows in-place editing.
Scene file edits are bidirectionally synchronized between the Retiam Studio in-browser editor and VS Code (or any external editor) via a file-watcher server.
`Ctrl+H` toggles clean mode which hides the editor UI, showing only the rendered canvas — useful for presentations.
**Description:** Full interactive event system that maps 2D/3D input events to scene entities via raycasting.
Scene-level input processor maintaining a spatial hash for fast hit-testing and dispatching events to entities.
An interactive draggable point that can be attached to entities for direct scene editing.
A built-in playback HUD with play/pause, seek bar, and speed control.

blocks.text: 28.5 npm run render / npx retiam render — Headless Video Render
Renders a scene headlessly to a video file (MP4 or WebM). This is the full offline production rendering pipeline.
The render pipeline uses a three-process architecture:

children.label: Vite
children.description: Development server on an automatic port

children.label: WebSocket
children.description: Each frame returns to Node.js on port 5001

items: **Deterministic** — Wall-clock time is fully decoupled. Each frame advances by exactly `1000 / fps` ms.
**Backpressure** — Browser halts and waits for `"ack"` WebSocket message before rendering the next frame, preventing memory exhaustion.
**Raytracing** — When raytracing is enabled, the simulation clock freezes and runs the full `rtMaxAccumulation` accumulation passes before extracting the frame.
**Auto port resolution** — If port 5173 is in use, Vite automatically finds the next free port.

blocks.code:
# Basic render (uses ratiam.config.js settings)
npx retiam render src/MyScene.ts

# Render at 4K 60fps
npx retiam render src/scenes/MyScene.ts -w 3840 -h 2160 -f 60

# Render with max duration override (10 seconds)
npx retiam render src/scenes/MyScene.ts -d 10000

# Render with raytracing enabled
npx retiam render src/scenes/3DScene.ts --raytrace

# Shortcut (defaults to render)
npx retiam src/MyScene.ts

blocks.text: The Input Virtualization system records all user interactions (mouse, keyboard, scroll) and replays them deterministically during headless rendering.

blocks.code:
# Step 1: Start the dev server
npm run dev

# Step 2: Open browser, navigate to http://localhost:5173
# Step 3: Start recording
#   macOS:         Command + Option + R
#   Windows/Linux: Control + Alt + R

# Browser console shows: 🔴 [InputRecorder] Recording started...

# Step 4: Perform interactions (orbit camera, drag objects, scroll, press keys)

# Step 5: Stop recording — press the same shortcut again
#   Browser console shows: ⏹️ [InputRecorder] Stopped. Captured X input events.
#   Browser auto-downloads: interactions.json

# Render with recorded interactions
npx retiam render src/MyScene.ts --replay interactions.json

# Override resolution when replaying
npx retiam render src/MyScene.ts --replay interactions.json -w 1920 -h 1080

items: All spatial coordinates are **normalized to [0.0, 1.0]** relative to canvas bounds during recording
These normalized coordinates are **remapped to the target resolution** during replay (resolution-independent)
Timestamps are **offset-corrected** — recording start time is subtracted so replay always begins at `time = 0`
Both `MouseEvent` and `PointerEvent` types are **dual-dispatched** with native DOM bubbling to reach all listeners
`movementX` / `movementY` deltas are **manually synthesized** from frame-to-frame coordinate differences
